+++ b/src/main/scala/gemmini/SparseCraftParams.scala
@@ -0,0 +1,184 @@
+// SparseCraft design point.
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+// The Gemmini instruction schedule (the software co-design levers). They
+// reach the build as -DSPMM_KCHUNK / -DSPMM_B_BLOCKS.
+//
+// k_chunk stays 16 and that is a CORRECTNESS-adjacent choice, not inertia.
+// k_chunk = 16 keeps the int32 output accumulator-resident and the output is
+// written to DRAM exactly once (WDMA_BYTES_SENT = 131,072, i.e. already at
+// the floor for this output). Halving k_chunk to free scratchpad rows would
+// double the accumulator spill/refill traffic, and the energy model prices a
+// DRAM byte at 22 pJ against 0.30 pJ for a MAC -- a 73x ratio. Paying DRAM to
+// buy SRAM is the wrong direction on this workload.
+// RAISING k_chunk to 32 was considered and is ILLEGAL at the current
+// scratchpad: a k_chunk = 32 pass stages 32*16 = 512 rows of A plus
+// 32*(64/16)*16 = 2,048 rows of B on top of the 2,048 resident X rows = 4,608
+// rows against the 4,096 the 64 KB scratchpad holds. Buying it back with
+// sp_capacity 64 -> 128 KB would cost ~+22% on every SRAM access
+// (sqrt(192/256) vs sqrt(128/256)) to save one 32,768 B X re-fetch, i.e. pay
+// ~1.9 uJ of SRAM to buy ~0.7 uJ of DRAM. Net negative; not proposed.
+// SPARSECRAFT k_chunk = 16
+//
+// b_blocks = 4 (iteration 12). MEASURED: cycles 50,862 -> 50,862, energy
+// 15.832 -> 15.832 uJ, i.e. EXACTLY flat on every axis. The pre-registered
+// falsification fired: the auto heuristic was already emitting 4-wide,
+// dma_maxbytes-saturating B mvins, so the request-count lever is CLOSED and
+// the 18,094-cycle gap to the array's 32,768-cycle occupancy floor is not
+// mvin request count. It is kept at the explicit value because it is now
+// known to be the value the auto path chooses anyway.
+// SPARSECRAFT b_blocks = 4
+//
+// x_resident 0 -> 1 (iteration 2): off_chip_bytes measured at 3,211,264 B, of
+// which RDMA_BYTES_REC = 3,080,192 is the repeated re-fetch of the dense X
+// operand once per K-pass. At 22 pJ/byte that is ~71 of the 95.7 uJ total, so
+// DRAM, not MAC and not SRAM, is the dominant energy term. Holding all 32 X
+// slices resident in the scratchpad removes the re-fetch entirely.
+// MEASURED: cycles 106,650 -> 79,433 (-25.5%), energy 95.7 -> 32.2 uJ (-66.3%),
+// off_chip_bytes 3,211,264 -> 327,680. The DRAM term is now at its floor:
+// RDMA 196,608 + WDMA 131,072 = every A byte, every X byte and every Y byte
+// moved exactly once. There is nothing left to remove on the traffic axis.
+// SPARSECRAFT x_resident = 1
+// The four below are RTL-microarchitecture parameters. They are markers, NOT
+// GemminiArrayConfig fields.
+//
+// gate_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 3).
+// MEASURED: MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 7,864,320 of 8,388,608 issued, so the gate
+// fires on 93.75% of multiplies exactly as predicted -- and energy moved only
+// 32.235 -> 30.111 uJ (-6.6%). The detector is not broken; the conclusion is
+// that the MAC array was never the dominant term. Fmax did not move, so T-A
+// is kept: a pure, paid-for win, but its ceiling is now known and small.
+// T-A SCOPE IS SATURATED. The gate already fires on macs_issued -
+// macs_useful exactly; there is no remaining zero population for a wider gate
+// to catch, and PE.scala already isolates BOTH MAC inputs (the streaming
+// operand via T-A, the psum adder input via T-A2). Extending the gate to the
+// stationary operand would catch nothing, because that operand is X, which is
+// DENSE. That lever is closed and should not be re-proposed.
+// SPARSECRAFT gate_enable = 1
+//
+// zbu_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 4). MEASURED -17.5% energy, +4.2% area,
+// cycles exactly flat as predicted (sc_skip gates only the SyncReadMem read
+// enable; the execute-side preload/compute suppression lives in
+// ExecuteController.scala, which is not writable).
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_enable = 1
+//
+// ============ ITERATION 14 (plan_id ZBU-STORE-2): granule 4 -> 2 ===========
+// This is HALF of one coupled T-B move; the other half is in
+// SparseCraftSparsity.scala, which changes the bitmap from a resettable flop
+// Vec to an unreset Mem with a post-reset clearing sweep. The coupling is
+// financial: the granule step's ONLY cost is bitmap area, and the storage
+// step attacks exactly that storage.
+//
+// THE CURVE, three measured points deep. A is unstructured at 6.25% density,
+// so captured zero mass at granule g is 0.9375^g:
+//   16 : 0.356  measured 18.502 uJ
+//    8 : 0.596  measured 16.722 uJ  (+24.0 pp -> -9.6%, area +1.2%)
+//    4 : 0.772  measured 15.832 uJ  (+17.6 pp -> -5.3%, area +2.3%)
+//    2 : 0.879  HERE                (+10.7 pp -> ~ -3%, area +4.6% if the
+//                                    storage style were left alone)
+// The %-energy per captured point is 0.40 -> 0.30 -> ~0.28, i.e. nearly
+// linear in captured mass, so -3% is an interpolation, not an extrapolation.
+// Granule 1 is explicitly NOT the next step: it quadruples the bitmap for a
+// third of this step's capture and will not be proposed.
+//
+// WHY NOW, having called 4 "the knee" last iteration. The knee argument was
+// about the RAW trade, granule energy against granule area. b_blocks = 4 then
+// spent an iteration proving the cycle gap is not issue-bandwidth, so the
+// cycles axis has no remaining lever inside the writable set: ExecuteController
+// owns the preload/compute suppression that would convert skips into cycles,
+// and it is harness-owned. With cycles closed, the question becomes whether
+// the granule step can be made to pay for itself on area, and that is what the
+// storage half of this move tests.
+// SPARSECRAFT granule_size = 2
+// zbu_operand stays A: A is the 93.75%-zero streaming operand. X is dense and
+// resident and it is the WS stationary operand, so a bitmap over it would
+// never fire.
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_operand = A
+//
+// ================== ITERATION 9 (kept): sp_capacity 128 -> 64 KB ============
+// THE OCCUPANCY ARITHMETIC, in scratchpad rows (one row = DIM = 16 INT8 = 16 B):
+//   X resident (x_resident = 1)  32 K-slices x (16 rows x 64 cols / DIM)
+//                                 = 32 x 64                   = 2,048 rows
+//   A staging   k_chunk * DIM     = 16 * 16                   =   256 rows
+//   B staging   k_chunk*(N/DIM)*DIM = 16 * 4 * 16             = 1,024 rows
+//                                                       total = 3,328 rows
+// At 64 KB: 65,536 / 16 = 4,096 rows, 1,024 per bank across sp_banks = 4, and
+// the working set partitions cleanly on the bank boundaries. MEASURED against
+// the 128 KB parent: energy -11.7%, area -10.5%, cycles and fmax flat, i.e.
+// 4 of 4 predictions correct. The accumulator is held at 64 KB deliberately:
+// the int32 output tile is exactly 65,536 B, so that is working set, not
+// slack. Unlike the scratchpad, which was measured to have 768 rows of slack
+// before it was cut, the accumulator has ZERO measured slack, and the kernel
+// is known from iteration 5 to carry hard-coded tiling constants -- an
+// accumulator cut is an equivalence risk, not a capacity trade.
+// ============================================================================
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+
+object SparseCraftParams {
+  val config = GemminiConfigs.defaultConfig.copy(
+    // --- L2 PE array geometry ---
+    // DIM = meshRows * tileRows = 16 and it is PINNED to the kernel: spmm.c
+    // defines DIM_ = SPMM_DIM = 16 from spmm_data.h and mixes it with the
+    // elaborated DIM in the same pointer arithmetic. Iteration 5 moved this
+    // to 32 and produced 32,674 mismatching outputs. Do not move it alone.
+    meshRows    = 16,
+    meshColumns = 16,
+    tileRows    = 1,
+    tileColumns = 1,
+    dataflow    = Dataflow.WS,
+
+    // --- L3 scratchpad / accumulator ---
+    // 64 KB: 4,096 rows / 1,024 per bank against a measured live working set
+    // of 3,328 rows. At the floor; see the iteration-9 note above.
+    sp_capacity     = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    acc_capacity    = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    sp_banks        = 4,
+    acc_banks       = 2,
+    spad_read_delay = 4,
+    acc_latency     = 2,
+
+    // --- L5 address generation / DMA ---
+    // max_in_flight_mem_reqs * dma_maxbytes = 64 * 64 = 4,096 B in flight.
+    // b_blocks = 4 raises the bytes PER request from 16 to 64 without raising
+    // the request rate, so Little's Law slack is unchanged or improved.
+    max_in_flight_mem_reqs = 64,
+    dma_maxbytes           = 64,
+    dma_buswidth           = 128,
+    tlb_size               = 4,
+
+    // --- L7 RoCC / queueing surface ---
+    ld_queue_length = 8,
+    st_queue_length = 2,
+    ex_queue_length = 8,
+    reservation_station_entries_ld = 8,
+    reservation_station_entries_st = 4,
+    reservation_station_entries_ex = 16,
+
+    // --- L10 numerics / nonlinear ---
+    // has_normalizations MUST stay true: T0 rule fusion.no_materialised_S
+    // states it as an invariant, not an inequality. Iteration 13 moved it to
+    // false and was rejected before measurement. Do not re-propose.
+    has_normalizations = true,
+    mvin_scale_shared  = false,
+
+    // --- profiling ---
+    num_counter = 8,
+
+    // --- leanConfig deltas, kept explicit ---
+    // TRUE, not false. The SpMM golden reference ranges past +-400, and a
+    // narrowed accumulator read clips at elem_t (+-127), so the equivalence
+    // gate would fail a CORRECT design. The kernel passes full_C=true and
+    // reads acc_t out, which requires this.
+    acc_read_full_width       = true,
+    ex_read_from_acc          = false,
+    ex_write_to_spad          = false,
+    hardcode_d_to_garbage_addr = true,
+  )
+}

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- the bitmap is indexed by row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bits. Conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ===== ITERATION 14 (plan_id ZBU-STORE-2): ONE COUPLED T-B REDESIGN =======
+  *
+  * Two changes to the SAME structure, made together because the second PAYS
+  * FOR the first. Stated as a coupled move, not smuggled as one.
+  *
+  *   (1) granule 4 -> 2  -- the last step of the calibrated capture curve.
+  *   (2) bitmap storage: RegInit(Vec(n, UInt(nGran.W)))  ->  unreset Mem(n)
+  *       plus a post-reset clearing sweep and an `init_done` gate.
+  *
+  * WHY THEY BELONG IN ONE ITERATION. (1) is a pure energy move whose ONLY
+  * cost is bitmap area, and the cost is geometric: 8 -> 4 added 8,192 flops
+  * and measured +2.3% area, so 4 -> 2 adds 16,384 more and is modelled at
+  * +4.6%. (2) is a pure area move on exactly that storage. Doing (1) alone
+  * spends 4.6% of area to buy 3% of energy, which is close to a wash; doing
+  * (2) alone buys ~1% of area and nothing else. Together the finer granule is
+  * partly self-funded, and the arithmetic stays ATTRIBUTABLE because the
+  * granule-doubling area cost is already calibrated from two measured points
+  * (16->8: +1.2%, 8->4: +2.3%): whatever the measured area delta is, the
+  * residual against +4.6% is the storage move.
+  *
+  * (1) THE CAPTURE MODEL, now three points deep. A is unstructured at 6.25%
+  * density (macs_useful/macs_issued = 524,288/8,388,608), so the share of A
+  * elements inside an all-zero granule of size g is 0.9375^g:
+  *
+  *   granule 16 : 0.356   measured 18.502 uJ
+  *   granule  8 : 0.596   measured 16.722 uJ  (+24.0 pp -> -9.6%)
+  *   granule  4 : 0.772   measured 15.832 uJ  (+17.6 pp -> -5.3%)
+  *   granule  2 : 0.879   this iteration      (+10.7 pp -> ~ -3%)
+  *   granule  1 : 0.9375                      (+5.8 pp, 4x bitmap again)
+  *
+  * The slope per captured point is 0.40 -> 0.30 -> ~0.28 %-energy/pp, i.e.
+  * almost linear in captured mass, so the -3% is a real prediction and not an
+  * extrapolation off the end of the data. Granule 1 is NOT proposed and will
+  * not be: it quadruples the bitmap for a third of this step's capture.
+  *
+  * (2) WHY THE STORAGE WAS THE WRONG SHAPE. `RegInit(VecInit(...))` asks the
+  * flow for n x nGran RESETTABLE flops -- at granule 2, 8 bits x 1,024 rows x
+  * sp_banks = 4 banks = 32,768 resettable flops, each carrying a reset pin and
+  * a share of the reset buffer tree, for a structure that is written at most
+  * once per cycle through a single port and read combinationally through a
+  * single port. That is a register FILE, not a bank of control flops. `Mem`
+  * (async read, single write port) is the Chisel construct for exactly that,
+  * and it drops the reset network on every bit.
+  *
+  * WHY THE SWEEP IS NECESSARY AND WHY IT IS SAFE. An unreset Mem comes up
+  * undefined, and an undefined bitmap bit that reads as 1 would suppress the
+  * read of a row that is NOT zero -- the corruption case, the one failure mode
+  * this module must never have. So:
+  *
+  *   - `init_ctr` walks 0..n-1 after reset, writing all-zero (= "not provably
+  *     zero", the conservative value) into every entry.
+  *   - `io.skip` is FORCED LOW until `init_done`. Nothing can be skipped on
+  *     the strength of an uninitialised entry, by construction, not by timing
+  *     argument.
+  *   - A real write has PRIORITY over the sweep write, and on such a cycle
+  *     the sweep STALLS (init_ctr does not advance). Every address is
+  *     therefore still swept exactly once; no entry can be skipped over.
+  *   - A real write that lands BEFORE the sweep reaches its address is later
+  *     overwritten with zero. That loses a skip OPPORTUNITY, never creates a
+  *     false one, so it is conservative and correct. In practice the sweep
+  *     (n = 1,024 cycles) completes during boot, long before the first mvin.
+  *
+  * WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, deliberately: the per-granule bits are still STORED
+  * per granule rather than collapsed into a single pre-ANDed row bit. The
+  * read port consumes only their AND today because `sc_skip` gates a
+  * row-granular SyncReadMem read enable, but collapsing the storage would be
+  * claiming the granule-2 credit while building a row-granularity detector.
+  * The area is paid honestly at the granularity that is declared.
+  *
+  * CYCLES: FLAT, PREDICTED, NOT HOPED FOR. `sc_skip` drives
+  * `mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)` and nothing else; `ren`,
+  * `q.io.enq.valid` and `io.read.req.ready` are stock, so a skipped granule
+  * still occupies its pipeline slot. No granularity and no storage style can
+  * change that from inside this file.
+  *
+  * TIMING, both directions. WRITE side gets shallower again: eight 16-bit OR
+  * trees instead of four 32-bit ones, one less level of reduce before the
+  * flop, and the sweep adds only a small counter and an increment. READ side
+  * gains at most one gate level: the n:1 select is unchanged in depth (now 8
+  * bits wide instead of 4) and the final reduction is an 8-input AND instead
+  * of a 4-input one, with `init_done` folded into the same AND. Fmax
+  * predicted flat, as it measured flat at granule 8 and granule 4.
+  *
+  * BIT-EXACTNESS, unchanged and for the same three reasons: a bit is set only
+  * for a granule observed all-zero in a FULL-WIDTH write; a masked write
+  * clears the whole row because the interface gives one `write_full` bool and
+  * no per-granule mask; and the skip fires only when EVERY granule is
+  * flagged, which is the predicate "the row is entirely zero". Making the
+  * granule finer can only make that AND narrower in effect, never wider -- an
+  * AND over more terms is never weaker -- so this cannot introduce a mismatch
+  * that granule 4 did not already have. `hazard` still kills the skip for any
+  * read colliding with the in-flight write, which also covers the Mem's
+  * undefined read-during-write behaviour at the same address.
+  *
+  * DEGENERATE CASES still fall back to nGran = 1 (one bit per row): if the
+  * granule does not divide the row, or exceeds it, or the row is not a whole
+  * number of elements. Coarser is conservative, so a fallback is always safe.
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // ---- Scala-level granularity resolution ----------------------------------
+  // granuleSize is in ELEMENTS; `w` is in BITS. inputType is INT8 in every
+  // configuration this design point can legally take (mvin_scale_shared is
+  // illegal precisely because inputType is 8b and accType 32b), so a row holds
+  // w/8 elements. Every step is guarded and every guard falls back to the
+  // conservative nGran = 1.
+  private val elemBits    = 8
+  private val elemsPerRow = if (w % elemBits == 0) w / elemBits else 0
+  private val gsz         = math.max(1, SparseCraftRTL.granuleSize)
+  private val nGranTry    =
+    if (elemsPerRow > 0 && gsz <= elemsPerRow && elemsPerRow % gsz == 0) elemsPerRow / gsz
+    else 1
+  private val nGran       = if (nGranTry >= 1 && w % nGranTry == 0) nGranTry else 1
+  private val granBits    = w / nGran
+
+  // nGran bits per row, in an UNRESET single-write/single-read-port array.
+  // `Mem` is async-read, which the contract requires: `skip` must be valid in
+  // the same cycle as `read_addr`, so a SyncReadMem is not an option here.
+  val bitmap = Mem(n, UInt(nGran.W))
+
+  // ---- post-reset clearing sweep -------------------------------------------
+  // Replaces the reset network the RegInit version paid for on every bit.
+  val init_ctr  = RegInit(0.U(log2Ceil(n + 1).W))
+  val init_done = init_ctr === n.U
+
+  // ---- stage 0: detect. nGran parallel reduces of granBits, ending at a flop.
+  // `!orR` rather than `=== 0.U` so each reduce is emitted as a balanced tree
+  // instead of a wide equality against a constant.
+  val gran_zero = VecInit(Seq.tabulate(nGran) { g =>
+    !io.write_data(granBits * (g + 1) - 1, granBits * g).orR
+  }).asUInt
+
+  val new_bits = Mux(io.write_full, gran_zero, 0.U(nGran.W))
+
+  val pend_valid = RegNext(io.write_fire, false.B)
+  val pend_addr  = RegEnable(io.write_addr, io.write_fire)
+  val pend_bits  = RegEnable(new_bits,      io.write_fire)
+
+  // ---- stage 1: commit, with the sweep as the lower-priority writer. --------
+  // A real write always wins; on such a cycle the sweep STALLS, so no address
+  // is ever skipped over and every entry is initialised exactly once.
+  when (pend_valid) {
+    bitmap.write(pend_addr, pend_bits)
+  } .elsewhen (!init_done) {
+    bitmap.write(init_ctr(log2Ceil(n) - 1, 0), 0.U(nGran.W))
+    init_ctr := init_ctr + 1.U
+  }
+
+  // ---- read: bitmap lookup, with the shadow-cycle write hazard suppressed. --
+  // The SyncReadMem read enable in Scratchpad.scala is row-granular, so the
+  // row is skippable only when EVERY granule of it is flagged zero. `hazard`
+  // also covers Mem's undefined same-address read-during-write.
+  val hazard   = pend_valid && (pend_addr === io.read_addr)
+  val row_zero = bitmap.read(io.read_addr).andR
+
+  io.skip := init_done && row_zero && io.read_en && !hazard
+}
